context:
HarborLink is a fictional public-library consortium reconciling patron accounts across five independently managed libraries. An entity means a person, not a household or a borrowing card. There are 1.8 million rows. Libraries issue local card numbers; two libraries recycle numbers after account closure. Names and addresses are usable inside the consortium workspace but must not leave it. Family members often share an address and phone. There is no representative labeled pair set. The only existing “gold” file contains 240 support escalations chosen because someone complained, and it mixes confirmed duplicate cards with household conflicts.

The current implementation blocks on normalized surname plus postal district, computes a weighted string-similarity score, and merges connected components above a hand-picked threshold. The operations lead reports fewer duplicates but has no denominator or source-stratified estimate. A mistaken merge can expose another person's loan history; missed duplicates are inconvenient but reversible. Staff can review 100 cases per week. No row-level data or access to the implementation is provided here, and permission is limited to an offline design note; do not propose deploying merges.

Recommend the smallest defensible evidence-collection and evaluation plan before choosing a new threshold or method. Compare the present system to one credible alternative, account for candidate loss and entity outcomes, and explain what the complaint file can and cannot establish. State the unresolved facts that would change your recommendation, safe next steps, and criteria for an inconclusive result.
title: HarborLink membership reconciliation
